Miami at +132 shows 174 edge_bps versus a median of +123, with BetOnline and LowVig both sitting 9 points above the market midpoint. At plus money with genuine line value and the superior starter on the mound, this is a worthwhile underdog play.

ig_carousel_topic.topic: Why your win rate matters less than your ROI
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
You Can Win 54% of Your Bets and Still Lose Money.
Here's why win rate is the wrong number to chase.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors track wins and losses like a scoreboard.
54% sounds great. But if your average win pays -115 and your average loss costs -115, you're grinding backward.
The percentage alone tells you almost nothing.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
ROI is the number that actually matters.
ROI = net units divided by total units wagered.
A bettor going 48% at +200 average odds beats a bettor going 56% at -115 average odds. Every time.
Odds shape the outcome. Win rate just counts the games.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Worked example:
Bettor A: 54 wins, 46 losses, all at -110. Net: roughly -1.8u.
Bettor B: 46 wins, 54 losses, averaging +145 on wins, -110 on losses. Net: roughly +5.2u.
Bettor B wins less often. Bettor B makes more money.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
SmarterPicks runs at 54.4% win rate and +9.3% ROI across 504 graded picks this year.
Both numbers matter. ROI is the one that pays your bills.
Check the full ledger at smarterpicks.io.
